findings.title: Mobile modal length-counter light-mode lightness changed from 70% to 30%
findings.description: The light-theme branch of `.custom-message-length` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The dark branch still uses `$secondary` at 70%, and every other conversion in this diff keeps the original light value. This makes the counter text much darker than the original design in light mode.

findings.title: Desktop topic-post reply-count light-mode lightness changed from 30% to 70%
findings.description: In the `a` rule nested under the post-summary block, the light-theme value was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. A 70% lightness is much paler than the original 30%, so link text in light mode becomes washed out.

findings.title: Desktop user-card `.name` light-mode lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.description: The `.name` rule's light-theme colour was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. It now matches `.title` and no longer matches the original name emphasis. The same wrong substitution appears in `mobile/user.scss:497`.

findings.title: Mobile user-card `.name` light-mode lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.description: The `.name` rule's light-theme colour was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, which makes the username lighter than the original design. This is the same slip as the desktop `.name` rule.

findings.title: Mobile topic-post `h3` light-mode lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.description: The `h3` rule's light-theme colour was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. The dark branch still uses `$secondary` at 80%, so the heading goes from near-black to mid-grey in light mode. The other `h3` and `.number, i` rules in the same diff keep 20%.
